description_en: Birth of Marcus Licinius Crassus into a wealthy senatorial family in Rome.
Crassus flees to Hispania during the Marian-Cinnan proscriptions; his father and brother are killed.
Crassus raises troops and joins Sulla in the civil war against the Marians.
Crassus appointed commander against Spartacus after several Roman defeats.
Crassus defeats Spartacus at the Battle of the Silarus River. Crucifixion of 6,000 survivors along the Appian Way.
Crassus elected consul for the first time, serving alongside Pompey.
Formation of the First Triumvirate: Crassus, Pompey, and Caesar form an informal political alliance.
The triumvirs meet at Luca to renew their alliance and divide provincial commands.
Crassus elected consul for the second time, again with Pompey as colleague.
Crassus departs for Syria as governor and launches invasion of Parthia.
Battle of Carrhae: Crassus is decisively defeated by the Parthian general Surena.
location: Carrhae, Parthian Empire (near modern Harran, Turkey)

description_en: Death of Crassus at Carrhae; circumstances of his death are disputed in ancient sources.
